title: The infer keyword and type extraction
hook: infer lets you capture a type variable inside a conditional type — the compiler extracts the return type of a function, the element type of a Promise, or the parameter list from a callback. Awaited, ReturnType, and Parameters are all built on infer.

blocks.text: **infer** appears only in the **extends** clause of a **conditional type**: `T extends SomeShape<infer U> ? U : never`. The compiler **infers** what `U` must be for the match to succeed and binds `U` for use in the true branch. It is type-level pattern matching — extract the inner type from a wrapper. Built-in utilities **ReturnType**, **Parameters**, **Awaited**, and **ConstructorParameters** are implemented with infer in lib.d.ts.

entries.plainDefinition: Declares a type variable to be inferred from a pattern match in a conditional type.
entries.example: T extends Promise<infer U> ? U : T

entries.plainDefinition: T extends U ? X : Y — resolves based on whether T is assignable to U.
entries.example: type IsString<T> = T extends string ? true : false

entries.plainDefinition: Pulling a component type out of a larger type expression.
Recursively unwraps Promise layers using nested infer.

blocks.text: Library authors use infer to build ergonomic wrappers: extract event map keys from a handler object, unwrap Redis client method return types, or infer API response shapes from fetch wrappers. LeetCode/Reddit senior TypeScript threads ask you to implement ReturnType or Awaited from scratch. Without infer, you would need manual overloads for every function signature — unmaintainable.

blocks.title: infer only in conditional true branch
blocks.body: infer U is scoped to the conditional where it appears. Multiple infer in one clause must not conflict — compiler unifies or errors.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Match pattern
items.body: T extends Promise<infer U> — does T look like Promise<Something>?

items.title: Bind inferred type
items.body: Compiler sets U to the inner type — e.g. string for Promise<string>.

items.title: No match
items.body: Take false branch — often never or T unchanged.

snippet.label: ReturnType and Parameters — infer from function shape
snippet.explanation: Line 1: infer R captures return type from any callable T. Line 2: infer P captures tuple of parameters. Line 9: typeof loadUser preserves function type for extraction.

snippet.label: Awaited — recursive infer unwrap
snippet.explanation: Lines 3–6: match thenable shape, infer fulfillment callback parameter V, recurse. Line 8: double-wrapped Promise unwraps to string — same idea as lib.es5 Awaited.

snippet.label: Production — extract event handler map
snippet.explanation: Lines 1–9: typed pub/sub. Line 12: advanced infer with extends constraint on infer P — extracts which event key matches payload shape.

snippet.label: Failure mode — infer in wrong position
snippet.explanation: Line 2: syntax error — infer must be inside T extends ... ? ... : .... Line 5: correct — extract array element type.

blocks.title: Expecting infer at runtime
blocks.body: infer resolves during type checking — erased in emitted JS. Runtime needs typeof checks or schemas.

blocks.title: Overly loose thenable match
blocks.body: Matching any object with then() can false-positive — Awaited uses a specific signature pattern.

blocks.text: Implement ReturnType, Parameters, Awaited in interview. Follow-up: infer in tuple destructuring `T extends [infer A, infer B] ? ...`, infer in recursive conditional for DeepPartial, covariant infer positions. Read lib.es5.d.ts Awaited source. Distributive conditionals apply when T is naked union — infer distributes per member. Production: wrap fetch client with generic inferring JSON type from endpoint map.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot write ReturnType with infer. Saying infer runs at runtime. Putting infer outside conditional. Not knowing Awaited is recursive infer.

interviewTakeaways: infer captures a type variable in conditional type extends clause.
ReturnType: T extends (...args: never[]) => infer R ? R : never.
Awaited recursively infers fulfillment type from thenable.
60s: infer is pattern match at type level. Extract return, params, Promise inner. Compile time only. Implement ReturnType and Awaited as interview drill.
Follow-up: distributive conditional with infer over union.
commonPitfalls: Weak: infer outside conditional — syntax error.
Weak: expecting runtime behavior — types erase.
Strong: 'infer U in extends pattern. ReturnType infers R. Awaited recurses thenable infer V. Read lib.d.ts.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript typeof and instanceof narrow at runtime — infer is the compile-time analog for type-level extraction from signatures.
Awaited<T> in lib.es5 is the canonical production use of recursive infer for Promise unwrapping.
